notebook:
PLAN: Retain the five-column C5/C4/C3/C6-paraffin blend core, but make the two C4/C5 and C5/C6 splits strip hard with high boil-up and much cheaper reflux. First obtain four saleable blends, then cut stages/duties and prune low-value branches.
The existing root already makes a clean C5- overhead but lets enough N-pentane into B to ruin the C6-paraffin blend; high root boil-up should fix this. T likewise leaves 25% N-butane in TB, so high boil-up rather than more stages is needed. TT already makes a qualifying C4 blend. TTT needs more reflux to keep ethane out of its C3 tops and more boil-up to keep isobutane out of C3 bottoms. B needs sharper recovery of C6 paraffins overhead. Lower pressure drop to 0.1 to improve relative volatility; light-column refrigeration remains a major cost to reduce later.

note: Reset the front end to low boil-up so C6 stays in the bottoms, sharpen the C4/C5 split, and prune the low-value C3 train.

High boil-up (12-14) was a costly mistake: it vaporized C6 into root tops and made root cost $422M. Use boil-up ~3 at root and T. TT needs enough reflux to retain C5 and enough boil-up to strip N-butane overhead. B at 60/6/8 previously cost $121M and is retained to recover C6 overhead. Current TB is already near 95% C6 paraffins, so cleaner feed should qualify. TTT is pruned: its $88M cost only generated $142M but prevents a simple blend flowsheet.

note: Prune the costly heavy branch and sharpen the three controlling cuts so the valuable C4 and C5 blends can actually sell.
notebook:

The prior root/T settings were far too sloppy: T contained 189 mol/s C5 and TB contained 181 C5, so no blend could qualify. B cost $290M without revenue and is now pruned. C4+C5 blends are worth about $805M/yr, versus only ~$58M for C3, so focus on those. Raising dp to 0.25 should reduce refrigeration cost. TT at 40/8/4 cost only $9M, so a sharper 60-stage version should remain cheap.

Potential revenue is about $498M C5 + $183M C4 + $58M C3. Peer R70 proves high boil-up works: TT 60/12/20 yielded 98% C5 and TTT 60/20/10 yielded 97% C4. My cascade is one column shorter, so T needs strong stripping to send all C4 overhead and TT needs strong stripping/reflux to send C3 overhead. Keep dp=0.25 to avoid R70's much higher refrigeration costs.
